brief.situation: You are the on-call security analyst for Pell & Rowe Fabrication, a fictional manufacturer with 120 staff. At 02:10 the EDR raises a critical alert: files on FS01, the shared file server, are being renamed to .lkr. Work the incident: contain it, keep the evidence, get the attacker out, recover the data, and report.
handover: FS01 holds every share; BK01 takes a nightly backup at 23:00; a weekly copy goes to an offline vault (six days old tonight). The stated recovery point objective is 24 hours.
The EDR agent can network-isolate a host and capture memory remotely.
howItWorks: Each task takes analyst time: choose it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes that task takes. Encryption and the attacker keep going on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you declare the incident contained, you notify, write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the incident record: the order you contained, preserved, eradicated and recovered in, and why that order.

parts.label: Containment
parts.criteria: Isolating FS01 at once stops encryption; network isolation is preferred to powering off because it keeps memory (power down only if a host cannot be disconnected, #StopRansomware Guide); the patient-zero workstation and the abused account are part of containment.
parts.modelAnswer: I network-isolated FS01 through the EDR agent as soon as triage confirmed ransomware, which stopped the encryption and kept memory for capture; powering off is only for a host that cannot be disconnected. I disabled svc_backup and isolated WS-ACCT07, where the attacker started.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.criteria: Memory before disk (order of volatility), a disk image before any wipe, hashes and chain of custody.
parts.modelAnswer: Before rebuilding I captured FS01's memory, then a disk image, recording hashes and who handled each, because memory is lost first and the wipe destroys the rest.

parts.label: Recovery
parts.criteria: Eradicate before recovering (disable the account, isolate every touched host) so the clean server is not reinfected; check the backup for indicators before restoring (NIST RC.RP-03); prefer the newest clean copy that meets the RPO.
parts.modelAnswer: Only after the attacker's access was cut did I rebuild FS01 and restore last night's backup, scanned for the indicators first, which meets the 24-hour recovery point and does not bring the attacker back.

backupsLost.label: Backups destroyed
backupsLost.narrative: The attacker reached BK01 and deleted the nightly backups. Only the weekly offline copy is left: six days of drawings and orders are gone, beyond the 24-hour recovery point.

reinfected.label: Reinfected during recovery
reinfected.narrative: FS01 was restored while the attacker still had a way in, and encryption started again on the clean server.

evidenceLost.label: Evidence wiped before it was collected
evidenceLost.narrative: FS01 was wiped with no image or memory capture, so no one can say what the attacker took or left behind, and the insurer and the FBI have nothing to work with.

stillIn.label: Closed with the attacker still in
stillIn.narrative: The incident was closed while {isNull(acctDisabledAt) ? "svc_backup was still enabled" : not wsIsolated ? "WS-ACCT07 was still beaconing out" : "the attacker still had a session on BK01"}.

contained.label: Contained, preserved and restored clean
contained.when: documented and not isNull(fsContainedAt) and timeAt(fsContainedAt) <= containWindow and spread <= containSpread and not isNull(evidenceAt) and not memLost and not evidenceDestroyed and restored == "nightlyScanned"
contained.narrative: Encryption stopped at FS01, the attacker never reached the backups, the evidence is in the case file, and last night's data is back after a scan.

containedLate.label: Contained, with spread or a costly recovery
containedLate.narrative: The attacker is out, but containment came late, BK01 was reached, the evidence is partial, or the recovery cost days of work.

time_up.label: Time up
time_up.narrative: The run reached its time limit with no incident record.

reasoningCriteria.label: Written order of containment, evidence and recovery

expertPath.text: Triage: ransomware started by svc_backup from WS-ACCT07. Network-isolate FS01 with the EDR agent.
Disable svc_backup, isolate WS-ACCT07, escalate to the incident commander.
Check where svc_backup logged on (BK01 untouched); capture memory, then a disk image; block the C2 address.
Rebuild FS01; restore last night's backup after scanning it; report to leadership, legal, the insurer, the FBI and CISA.

contained.headline: Good: contained, preserved, restored clean
contained.body: Isolation stopped the encryption, the attacker never reached the backups, and you rebuilt only after the evidence was kept and every path was cut.

containedLate.headline: Contained, at a cost
containedLate.body: The attacker is out. The criteria show what cost you: late isolation, a host reached, memory lost to a power-off, or days of data lost to an old copy.

backupsLost.headline: Backups destroyed
backupsLost.body: Attackers go for the backup server next. Cutting the account and the source workstation early, or isolating BK01 once it was reached, keeps the nightly backups.

reinfected.headline: Reinfected
reinfected.body: Restoring before eradication, or from a backup the attacker touched without checking it, brings the attacker back (#StopRansomware: take care not to re-infect clean systems).

evidenceLost.headline: Evidence wiped
evidenceLost.body: A rebuild before an image destroys what the insurer, the FBI and your own root-cause work need. Capture memory, then disk, then rebuild.

stillIn.headline: Closed too soon
stillIn.body: An enabled svc_backup, a beaconing WS-ACCT07 or a session on BK01 is a way back in. Account for every means of persistent access before you close (CISA).

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Confirm ransomware, then network-isolate FS01 (power off only if it cannot be disconnected), disable the abused account and isolate the patient-zero workstation, and escalate. Check where the account logged on and isolate anything it reached. Capture memory and a disk image before any wipe. Rebuild, restore the newest backup that meets the RPO after scanning it, report to leadership, legal, the insurer and the FBI and CISA, and do not pay.
